entries.title: HH Spearheads on Foreheads
entries.description:
[overview]
This build is great at single target, not very good at AoE but it does have a decent amount of cleave. You can move for the entire damage rotation though, so you can keep yourself safe in boss encounters or while kiting elites across the countryside in the open world.

[talents]
HH tree: Hunting for Sport, you should have near 100% uptime when you can set up and maintain your rotation. 20% armor pen is fantastic.
Barb tree: Savage Cadence and HH tree: Deep Fury are going to keep your Unbridled Rage up and available most of the time.

Barb tree: Outrage and Bloodthirsty, this is your big cooldown for a huge spike in damage. Once you get rolling and have enough crit you can keep it up for the duration of a fight.

HH tree: Gutspiller>Guts Splatter>To the Bone, this section of talents provide some great synergy that help you and your party both. Splatter gives you another source of 20% armor pen. To the Bone stacks a 20% armor sunder on the target that benefits the entire party.
HH tree: Legacy of Amani, great bonus damage when you get lucky. 
HH tree: Manhunter, you do 10% more damage vs humanoids, and everyone in your group gets 3% more crit. Quality point spent.

HH tree: Berserker and Sen'Jin's Guidance, Sen'jin's is where your rotation will finally make more sense. It will reset your Berserker Axe just like your other spears, but is not on the same cool down as your Spear abilities. Berserker is another boost (similar to Legacy of the Amani) that you won't have to worry about maintaining, it will just come naturally with your rotation.

[rotation]
Open with Unbridled Rage and Gutspiller. Gut spiller should be maintained, but not clipped because the final tick will be a Guts Spilled tick for more damage and a 4% sunder. 

Swing between burning Berserker Axe stacks or using a spear until you have to reapply Gutspiller
Use your 3 stacks of Berserker Axe. Berserker axe is going to reset after every spear while you are Enraged (should be 100%)
Javelin Toss (Sen'jin's guidance turns your throw weapon into a spear) does the most damage of the spears and is off the spear cooldown.
Headhunter's spear, decent damage, has no energy cost and bumps your energy up by 30%. Use this to keep from being energy starved. 

**the TL;DR**: Pop Outrage and macro in your Troll racial and trinkets.

**Single Target** - keep Unbridled Rage and Gutspiller rolling. Rotation starts 3 Berserker Axe > Javelin > 3 Berserker Axe > Headhunter's  spear and repeat the rotation.

For AoE - Carnage into Unbridled Rage then Spinning Axes into Gutspiller. 3 Berserker Axe > Impaling Spear > Onslaught if Carnage is down and you need to maintain energy > back to 3 berserker axe > Javelin and then repeat as best you can. You will run out of energy eventually and the real AoE classes will make you look silly anyways.

Maiming Spear is a utility for kiting and slowing down targets. 
Barbed spear is only better than Javelin if the target is being healed.

Impaling spear, decent AoE but has a wonky aiming mechanic similar to Cone of Cold or something. Make sure you are facing your target when you chuck it.

Sidenote, you can use your regular old Throw ability that everyone gets for a quick, no energy pop of damage. It works when you are standing still while spamming Berserker Axe. It is not on the same GCD as your abilities so you can just weave it in. Not much but I think its cool B)

entries.title: [user] PVP Hybrid Spearthrower
entries.description:
[overview]
A highly mobile, high burst damage, with incredibly good survivability build for the barb. This build allows you to kite most classes with ease while maintaining good dps uptime and bleeds on them, with practice you can kite multiple people as long as you have decent cooldown management.

End talents are a WIP as i constantly tweak and adjust the build, enjoy :D

[rotation]
Always start with an enrage, this build has many. Enrage procs the "You want axe?" talent that refreshes 3 charges of Berserker Axe that cost -%50 less energy.


## A good opener most of the time would be: **Unbridled Rage > Maiming Spear > 3x Berserker Axe > Gutspiller > Barbed Spear > 3x Berserker Axe** and they are usually dead. 

Enrage is also used for Ancestral Roar, one of your main regen abilities, good A.R management will allow you to stay healthy for a lot longer, especially versus other ranged classes such as Rangers and Pyros.
If you find yourself getting in trouble, pop Warband and Defiance to help mitigate some of the incoming damage, you also have Battle Vigor to enrage yourself and gain an increased 40% max HP.

Once you are out of combat, the Ancestral Keg can be used in conjunction with a lot of heals, including your Grisly Meal, allowing barbs to go from 1% hp to full in around 3-5 seconds out of combat, a very underlooked tool of their kit.

Whirling Advance is an incredible mobility tool once you get used to its jankness. Paired with Onslaught, it allows us to traverse the BG with ease, allowing us to dip in and out of combat easily. Want to be a flag carrier? Go ahead, we can keep up with most Felsworns when you get the Forward Advance talent and with good energy regen. You can also Whirling Advance into a spellcaster to Headbutt them, then spin out to start your spear/axe combos.

Then there's Gutspiller, one of the most underrated abilites a Barb has. The damage from Guts Spilled is absolutely mental as the bleed procs can, and will, crit quite often. Try to maintain the debuff on enemies as much as possible, especially when you have Twirling Axes enabled as this will spread your bleed damage over anyone in the vicinity of your target.
Speaking of bleeds, it synergizes extremely well with this build due to the higher crit chance we get with our spears from it, allowing you to have incredible burst once a target is bleeding.

entries.title: Headhunter PvP build
entries.description:
[overview]
A lot of what’s built into this talent set up is maxing uptime on guts spilled and berserker axe. Cycling your energy maintenance abilities will allow full uptime in unbridled rage while spamming berserker axe’s. This allows for born in blood to always be 2 stacked on you and healing for a lot per tick with brutal form. 

How I tend to open combat
Warband
On use/racial
Gut spiller
3 zerkers 
Maimed spear
3 zerkers
Throw weapon(sometimes depending on the class I will use berserker rush and spam headbutt before I get there)
Slow spear 

Rinse repeat

Fleshweaver is an Attonement Style Healer
This Class Uses Health, And Rage as it's main Resources.

After Extensive testing this is the best build i have come up with.

Made By Mortyy on Vol'jin

If you would like to join the Shrimp Gang community check out my friend Twitch.tv/Thighgapy

[talents]
The Reason We Skipped the Bottom Row Talents is as Follows
[Predator] Allows for your [Sanguine Rupture](coa-skill:bloodmage:800774) to do 10% more Critical Damage, and [Sanguine Mend](coa-skill:bloodmage:802310) to hit up to 2 targets instead of 1
Now if you Factor in you took the talent [Crimson Scion](coa-skill:bloodmage:806424) This is a very good combination allowing you to proc instant cast heals on up to 2 party members next to each other. 
By Dealing Damage with any Direct Damage abilities You can Proc [Crimson Scion](coa-skill:bloodmage:806424) for instant cast [Sanguine Mend](coa-skill:bloodmage:802310) a few examples of these abiltiies are [Sanguine Rupture](coa-skill:bloodmage:800774) , [Bloodmoon Blast](coa-skill:bloodmage:501607) , [Ravenous Strike](coa-skill:bloodmage:500123) , or [Claw Sweep](coa-skill:bloodmage:500169)
[Sanguine Mend](coa-skill:bloodmage:802310) is your main heal on the move.

We also Took [Adrenaline Boost] And [Flesh Foundry](coa-skill:bloodmage:704633) Because it Allows for us to increase our crit chance dramatically While Weaving in Cursed form abilities and allows us to fish for instant [Dark Liturgy](coa-skill:bloodmage:800781)  and allows us to keep up [Dark Essence] as long as [Dark Liturgy](coa-skill:bloodmage:800781) is active (Getting good at this will be extremely rewarding)

[rotation]
When Entering a Dungeon Apply These Buffs to your Party and to yourself
- Greater [Sanguinary Offering](coa-skill:bloodmage:706630)- Greater [Bloodthorns](coa-skill:bloodmage:802313)- [Blood Shield](coa-skill:bloodmage:504296)

Rotation
- [Sanguine Rupture](coa-skill:bloodmage:800774) To Generate Rage On Multiple Targets.
- [Crimson Tide](coa-skill:bloodmage:504282) is a good skill to use if you have Excess rage in a Aoe Pull Because it will apply bleeds on up to 10 enemies which can Proc  [Spice Of Life] This combined with [Raging Hunger] Allows for massive rage generation and Pooled vitality  in aoe scenarios it also adds [Waves of Blood] Which can also proc  [Excess Blood].
- [Ravenous Strike](coa-skill:bloodmage:500123) Quickest single target rage generator, Also Allows you to proc [Adrenaline Boost] to get a instant [Dark Liturgy](coa-skill:bloodmage:800781) Both [Ravenous Strike](coa-skill:bloodmage:500123) (single target) and [Claw Sweep](coa-skill:bloodmage:500169) (Aoe) Can trigger this. and since both of these are cursed form abilities you proc [Dark Essence] at a 100% up time
- [Claw Sweep](coa-skill:bloodmage:500169) This Ability Costs 22 rage it's a good ability to use in aoe pulls to trigger [Dark Essence] and [Adrenaline Boost], while in aoe pulls you can use this in conjunction with [Sanguine Rupture](coa-skill:bloodmage:800774) to fish for both [Adrenaline boost] and [Crimson Scion](coa-skill:bloodmage:806424)
-  [Adrenaline Boost] This is a Talent, When using any of your melee cursed form abilities, if you crit it allows you to cast [Dark Liturgy](coa-skill:bloodmage:800781) or [Bloodmoon Blast](coa-skill:bloodmage:501607) as an instant cast.
- [Dark Essence] This is a Talent, When you use any of your cursed form abilities it will trigger an aoe Hot on your party as long as [Dark Liturgy](coa-skill:bloodmage:800781) is active, if you actively melee weave you will have a 100% uptime on Hot's also triggering [Adrenaline Boost]  for the instant cast [Dark Liturgy](coa-skill:bloodmage:800781)
-  Casting [Dark Liturgy](coa-skill:bloodmage:800781) to apply [Blood Rituals](coa-skill:bloodmage:705729) is important so that you can use [Bloodmoon Blast](coa-skill:bloodmage:501607) for a party wide Heal while also generating rage (Single Target) While Stationary to avoid cleave mobs.
- Your Main Aoe heal is [Heartbreak](coa-skill:bloodmage:520314) This Costs 40 Rage.  If using this while Empowered it Gives 165 Attack Power/Spellpower To Party/Raid (Very good buff to keep up if you can fit it in.)
- Your main Single Target Heal is [Sanguine Mend](coa-skill:bloodmage:802310) This costs 20 Rage. If using this while Empowered it becomes a instant cast, and heals you for 50% of the heal value. Since we took [Predator] This ability now heals up to 2 people. and [Crimson Scion](coa-skill:bloodmage:806424) can proc when you do damage allowing you access to this ability as an instant cast.
- [Blood Veil] This is good to use Preemptively on a pull since it lasts 8 seconds or when your party is taking alot of damage, it shields them for 50% of incoming damage up to 1600 and gives you a bit of breathing room to generate rage or line up a [Heartbreak](coa-skill:bloodmage:520314) 
- [Fleshcraft](coa-skill:bloodmage:801952) This is your Panic button. It's Close to a lay on hands.
- [Shadow Vigil](coa-skill:bloodmage:806182) When someone in your party Rips threat or is taking alot of damage and they aren't a tank this will Give them an 8 second threat wipe.
- Before Using [Red Thirst](coa-skill:bloodmage:520493) Make sure you line up 10 stacks of pooled vitality and use [Heartbreak](coa-skill:bloodmage:520314) to Grant 165 attack power/Spellpower for 20 seconds. Combining this combo with [Infuse] Allows for Massive Damage for both you and your team.
- [Vampyr's Kiss](coa-skill:bloodmage:504275) applies a 2000 damage dot and instantly Gives you 30 Rage.
- [Blood Tap] Is a ability that Sacrafices some health for 50% of your maximum rage.
- [Animated Blood] When you have excess rage it is good to let these guys loose and put out some damage, they also heal you for 200 hp everytime each of them cast blood blast.
- [Lunge](coa-skill:bloodmage:500126) Good skill to close the gap on mobs so u can melee weave or if you need to catch up to tank 
- [Hypovolemic Shock](coa-skill:bloodmage:572305) This ability lowers the Attack power of an enemy by 265, and also removes a Enrage effect good to keep up on bosses if they are not immune.

entries.title: IMMORTAL TYRANT - Walking Fortress
entries.description:
[overview]
## Ever wanted to feel like a raid boss?

That's exactly what this build is about.

You're trading flashy burst damage for ridiculous survivability, allowing you to tank almost anything the game throws at you while still putting out enough DPS to stay relevant.

The build shines in every PvE scenario and can easily be adapted for PvP by replacing a couple of optional picks with Mana Burn.

Everything else is essentially mandatory. Every talent has a purpose and contributes to making the build as durable and consistent as possible.

If dying isn't part of your game plan, you've found the right build.

[talents]
This build focuses on consistency rather than burst damage. 
Every talent has been selected with one of four objectives:
- Increase survivability.
- Improve Felfury generation.
- Maximize Inner Demon uptime.
- Maintain strong threat while dealing competitive damage.

Many offensive talents were intentionally skipped in favor of defensive consistency. A dead tank deals no damage.
The Tyrant tree naturally provides excellent damage, allowing us to invest more heavily into mitigation without sacrificing clear speed.

**If you prefer a simpler rotation with one less button to manage, you can replace Tyrant's Gaze with Betrayer. While you'll lose some execute damage, Betrayer remains a solid alternative and is perfectly viable for players who value a smoother playstyle.**

[rotation]
### Multi-Target Rotation

**Hateforged Barrier** → **Burning Hatred or Blood of Mannoroth** → **Inner Demon** → **Felrend** → **Felrend** → **Sunder**  → **Sargeron Smite**

Use **Carve** whenever possible. Thanks to **Annuhilan Rituals**, a fully channeled **Carve** effectively costs only **1 Felfury**, making it extremely efficient. Follow it with **Fireball** to benefit from the empowered cast. The **Carve → Fireball** combo deals excellent AoE damage and should be used whenever you have the opportunity.

 ⚠️⚠️ **Warning:** The **Carve → Fireball** combo is a DPS gain, but it also comes with a survivability trade-off.⚠️⚠️

Because you're spending less Felfury with the combo**Felrend** and **Sargeron Smite**, you reduce your **Hateforged Barrier** uptime, gain fewer **Abyssal Conditioning** stacks, and spend more time channeling. If you're playing without a dedicated healer, I generally recommend sticking to the **Felrend + Sunder + Sargeron** rotation for much better consistency and survivability. See the discussion in the comments for a more detailed explanation.

Once an enemy drops below **35% Health**, prioritize **Tyrant's Gaze** to execute the target and quickly move on to the next enemy.

### Single-Target Rotation

The single-target rotation follows the exact same priority, with only two changes:

* Replace **Felrend** with **Twin Slice**.
* Replace **Sunder** with **Sargeron Smite**.

**Rotation:**

**Hateforged Barrier** → **Burning Hatred** → **Inner Demon** → **Twin Slice** → **Twin Slice** → **Sargeron Smite**

⚠️ **Never cast Sargeron Smite without Inner Demon active.**
 Doing so results in a massive DPS loss and significantly reduces the effectiveness of the build. Always make sure **Inner Demon** is active before using **Sargeron Smite**.

## 💥 Cooldowns

### Hateforged Barrier
Your most important defensive cooldown.
Keep it active as often as possible. Thanks to cooldown reduction, maintaining nearly permanent uptime is entirely achievable.

### Inner Demon
This build revolves around **Inner Demon**.
Never let it expire unless absolutely unavoidable.
Every aspect of your rotation is designed around maximizing its uptime.

### Burning Hatred
Primarily used to instantly generate Felfury and quickly reactivate **Inner Demon**.
Avoid using it immediately on every pull.

Instead, save it for:
* Long encounters.
* Large pulls.
* Recovering after losing Felfury.

### Blur
Reserved for boss mechanics or emergency situations.
Since **Blur** reduces your threat generation, always follow it with **Betray** to immediately recover aggro.

### Fel Bargain
Emergency button.
Only use it if your healer cannot keep you alive.
Without a Tinker in your group, this cooldown becomes significantly more dangerous.

[stats]
**Priority**

1. Hit Rating (until cap)
2. Agility
3. Stamina
4. Critical Strike
5. Haste

Agility is by far the strongest primary stat for this build, increasing both your offensive and defensive capabilities.

Because several abilities scale from weapon damage, using **two slow two-handed weapons** provides the highest overall performance.

Leather gear with Agility remains the best option.

[leveling]
Leveling as a Tyrant is extremely smooth and beginner-friendly. The spec has excellent survivability, allowing you to comfortably solo most quests and elite enemies without much difficulty.

Your main priority while leveling is to spam Felrend as your primary damage and threat ability while keeping Hateforged Barrier active whenever possible.

Although the build is capable of handling large pulls, don't get too greedy early on. Your gear won't be optimized yet, and overpulling can quickly overwhelm both you and your healer in dungeons.

Play it safe during the early levels, focus on maintaining your defensive abilities, and gradually increase your pull size as your gear and survivability improve.

By the time you reach higher levels and unlock the full build, you'll be able to comfortably chain large packs and fully take advantage of Tyrant's incredible durability.

[pvp]
The PvP version keeps almost the entire build unchanged.

The only recommended adjustment is replacing a few PvE-oriented talents with **Mana Burn**.

This allows you to heavily pressure healers and casters while maintaining the incredible survivability that makes Tyrant so powerful.


>_>

Tyrant truly shines as an objective-focused flag carrier. Your incredible survivability makes you extremely difficult to kill, allowing you to secure and transport flags with confidence.

While this build is perfectly capable of winning most 1v1 encounters, don't get baited into unnecessary fights. Your real value comes from playing the objective.

Capture bases, carry flags, waste the enemy team's time, and force them to commit multiple players just to bring you down. Winning the battleground is far more satisfying than chasing kills.

[tips]
# ❌ Common Mistakes
* Letting **Inner Demon** expire.
* Casting **Sargeron Smite** without **Inner Demon**.
* Forgetting to refresh **Hateforged Barrier**.
* Wasting **Burning Hatred** at the beginning of every fight.
* Using **Fel Bargain** too early.
* Using **Blur** without immediately following it with **Betray**.
* Ignoring **Tyrant's Gaze** below 35% Health.
* Focusing too much on DPS instead of maintaining defensive uptime.

# 💡 Advanced Tips
* Always start difficult pulls with **Hateforged Barrier** already active.
* Plan your **Burning Hatred** usage instead of treating it like a regular cooldown.
* Prioritize maintaining **Inner Demon** over squeezing in one extra offensive ability.
* Use **Felrend** and **Sunder** aggressively on large pulls to stabilize threat before your DPS unloads.
* Save **Blur** for predictable boss mechanics rather than random damage.
* A good Tyrant anticipates incoming damage instead of reacting once health starts dropping.
* **Tyrant's Gaze** is more than an execute—it helps reduce incoming damage by removing dangerous enemies from the fight faster.
* Don't be afraid to chain large pulls. This build truly shines when fighting multiple enemies at once, where its survivability and threat generation outperform most other tanks.

entries.title: Guardian Gladiator PvP optimal build
entries.description:
[overview]
PvP Gladiator build prioritizing utility, survivability, and burst damage. Cycling through strong, low CD offensive cooldowns for big burst damage as a win con to close out sustained fights.

[talents]
Clinch Brawler guarantees a Centurion Strike crit so try to play around that, using Net Shot and Chivalry for big burst damage on the opener. 

Calculated Strike allows your Spear Throw to do respectable damage along with the 50% MS effect which you'll usually look to take advanage of in the opener. Reprisal isn't really reliable against non-melee classes since polearm won't be proccing the ability itself very often. High weapon damage, slow swing speed weapons are preferred for Centurion Strike burst. Valiant Effort could  be replaced with something else if you don't find value in it. 

Always look to root and slow people inside Glorious Arena. Comboing the with Grand Entrance is more burst on top of your Net Shot + Chivalry + Centurion Strike crit rotation. Currently the Heroism talent is bugged, so I'm taking Close Combat atm. Standard being on GCD is still very nice to swap between them as needed. In pvp Valiance is used very often, but the stun resist banner is pretty great too in teamfights. In a 1v1 melee brawl you can't go wrong with the healing banner.

[rotation]
Ideal opener is Spear Throw -> Net Shot -> Standard of Valiance -> Chivalry -> Centurion Strike -> Glorious Arena -> Grand Entrance. Keep track of Glory stacks with Heroic Effort so you don't end up with Ram on a full CD while you're sitting on 3 Glory stacks. Try not to use Battle Rush in the opener if you don't have to, it's important to trade mobility with the opponent, so if you're using it in the opener when you don't have to you're a lot more liable to being kited. 

Don't forget Linebreaker. It basically works like Shattering Throw, breaking immunities and has a -25% armor reduction debuff with only a 1 minute cooldown. The armor debuff can be hard to play around, only lasting 5 seconds.

[stats]
Strength = Stamina ≥ Agi  Gladiator gets a lot of raw damage from strength, but agi is also a great stat that you can't go wrong with as it gives you a lot of benefits. Your main win con is playing around the Net Shot + Centurion Strike burst which has guaranteed crits built in. Having crit is still good though, your sustained damage becomes a real threat when Grand Entrance and Ram also start dealing big numbers.

[gear]
Conquest Point PvP gear can be bought at booty bay. Honor gear is bought at your main towns' (Orgimmar or Stormwind) PvP vendor. These pvp items have higher resilience and pvp power than bloodforged so make sure you get them. These vendors sell enchants too and PvP trinket as well.

[leveling]
Pull big with Tower Formation and a polearm, Centurion Strike and Broad Sweeps for big groups off adds. Raise Shield will be your primary way of getting Reprisal off since slow polearms can't proc it on it's own consistently enough.

[pvp]
You have a lot of defensives to cycle through. You're a lot better at fighting melee than ranged, so look to check those classes and use keep relevant banners up (slow, stun resist, or healing usually, sometimes disarm resist). Counter Stance is basically a full heal so long as you get parries off, you can use this against pets too for a free full heal. Turn the Blade against other melees, Brace against Barbarians in the opener is good to avoid their Stun + Crush combo.

Using a Standard of Spellwarding in the middle of a group of casters you can't go wrong with, either. It's a deceptively strong way for gladiator to find value in a teamfight.

[macros]
Here are all the macros I use, It's built to avoid having to avoid using an input on stance switching. 

#showtooltip Advance
/cast [stance:2/3] Line Formation
/cast Advance

#showtooltip Unyielding Stand
/cast [stance:1/3] Tower Formation
/cast Unyielding Stand

#showtooltip Battle Rush
/cast [stance:1/2] Assault Formation
/cast Battle Rush

#showtooltip Brace

/cast Brace

#showtooltip Turn The Blade

/cast Turn The Blade

#showtooltip Guard

/cast Guard

#showtooltip Knight's Calling

/cast Knight's Calling

#showtooltip Shield of Denial
/cast [stance:3] Tower Formation
/cast [stance:2] Shield of Denial
/cast [stance:1] Shield of Denial

#showtooltip Harrowing Melody
/cast [stance:2/3] Line Formation
/cast Harrowing Melody

#showtooltip Net Throw
/cast [stance:1/2] Assault Formation
/cast Net Throw

#showtooltip Counter Stance
/cast [stance:1/2] Assault Formation
/cast Counter Stance

#showtooltip Reflective Shield
/cast [stance:1/3] Tower Formation

#showtooltip Linebreaker

#showtooltip Raise Shield

#showtooltip Spear Throw

[tips]
Trade mobility with players, use your gap closers in response to their own mobility or CC. Don't waste advance, shrug it off, or battle rush if you don't need to. Do not Net Shot the same player immediately off cooldown; 15 seconds isn't enough time for CC DR to fade away, and they will only be rooted for 1-2 seconds. Spear Throw should be used before big bursts, as most classes have some form of sustain and will probably respond with big defensive buttons in response to your damage.

Standard of Spellwarding is a great utility option in big teamfights. Throw it in the middle of the enemy backline for free value if they have a lot of casters.

entries.title: Inspiration Guardian(PvE)
entries.description:
[overview]
Welcome to Hell! I mean inspiration guardian, you've made the right choice coming here. Overly complex combos, random procs that determine if you sit there doing nothing or deal moderate dmg levels. It's a blast!

Strengths
- Raid wide buffs(5% crit/5% haste/5% rep/10% crit/10% dmg/10% healing/10%haste/+35% ap as adaptive/+145 adaptive/+15% dmg/10% physical crit dmg)
- Good damage output 
- High survivability and mobility 
- AOE CC & CC Immunity 
Weakness
- Damage is very RNG
- Peak damage isn't very high
- Complexity and stance swapping can be a major turn off

[talents]
Most talents are pretty self explanatory going to discuss controversial ones

Feel free to swap Liberation for talents that may be useful for your group I.E. little drummer for stratholme
Inspiration Dissonance vs Song of steel. 
Song of steel cost 30 energy every 15 seconds and heavily slows down your combo. This is more useful in larger raids I.E. 20-40 man raids(it affects everyone in raid) or in heavy physical DPS comps. If you're doing dungeons/10 man raids, dissonance will give you and your party a lot more value especially if your group has more casters.

Voice of an Angel and Champion Presence - these are both extremely long CDs for very little return. For such a long cds we'll likely only get to use it once a fight it's not worth it compared to other options.

Valiant Warrior vs Grand Entrance - Grand Entrance can be a bit awkward to use, and although we stack strength making the AP values very attractive we also actively stack crit and are able to Empowered ram almost on CD. Along with the fact we don't have very high weapon scaling. After two ram procs Valiant Warrior will out value Grand Entrance.

Bannerman vs Echoes of War - Bannerman is currently bugged doing 0% extra damage on the initial tick and 300% extra damage(150% more for each banner) on every subsequent tick. Personally I run echoes of war, in a raid setting it can often be 2-5% of your raid members total damage contributing almost 4000dps by itself. Bannerman will give you a higher personal DPS output, and better dungeon damage.

[rotation]
We want to start most encounters in Line Formation this will allow us to open with **Harrowing Melody** and **advance**. Once we begin our rotation we want to swap and sit in **Assault stance** for the bonus crit and dmg.

**Jagged Reinforcement** when above 30% base crit(45% with banner + assault), **Weighted Reinforcement** when below this threshold.

We have a very simple opener 
Opener in question:
Advance + Standard of Supremacy/Valiance -> Harrowing Melody(run away after casting) + Battle drums + End Advance-> Assault formation + Charge -> Macro(hero's March +  Chivlary + Inspiring Presence) + Glorious Arena + CLICK THOSE DRUMS -> Priority Rotation 
This opener takes about 3 seconds.

The main idea behind our rotation is pop all our cds, spam Dragonslayer until we get empowered ram and look for reprisal procs. Having a fast weapon will help out a lot with getting enough reprisal procs to not be sitting at 0 energy doing nothing.

Single Target - Priority
0. Standard of Valiance
1. Buffs: Hero's March/Chivalry/Inspiring Presence/Song of steel/Battle Drums
2. Harrowing Melody
3. Dragonslayer(If 3 or more mobs)
4. Empowered Ram(Cast at 2 tempo stacks)
5. Reprisal(/Inspiring Presence(When below 50 energy)
6. Glorious Arena
7. Ballad of the Conqueror

Note on casting harrowing melody mid combat, to go from assault, cast harrowing melody, and back to assault cost 70 energy returning effectively 105 energy worth of ballad cast. Have at least 70 energy casting from assault. 

Try to cast linebreaker in line with harrowing melody, this reduces energy waste from stance swaping and greatly benefits boss damage.

Dungeon:
During Dungeons I suggest alternating between inspiring Presence and Hero's March on pulls. While stacking them all is good on big pulls, when during small pulls alternate. This will gives you the most uptime of buffs, while maximizing cds so every minute you can pop one of these. Chivalry can be thrown in when you have packs large packs or elites.

Battle Drums should be used on dungeon bosses, don't pop it on trash packs unless it includes a boss. When doing raids try to place drums pre-pull to reduce energy waste or use them how the opener demonstrates. Using them mid raid boss is currently not viable because map clutter makes it very hard to notice/click them so only use them in your opener or pre-pull.

Raid: 
You are responsible for taking banners, other supports should take the 1% hit and armor versions. **ALWAYS COMMUNICATE WITH OTHER SUPPORTS WHAT TALENTS THEY ARE BRINGING, DO NOT OVERLAP**

[stats]
Expertise(Up to cap) > Hit(Up to cap) > Strength > Critical Strike  > Haste > AP > Armor Pen > agility

Everything you have scales off AP so strength to scale, we have naturally high crit rate and crit damage so it's not vital but will greatly boost dps and make ram less RNG. Hit and expertise up to cap.

[gear]
For weapons, we want fast weapons with a lot of stats.  All of our scaling comes for AP, so weapon damage is negligible. Try to proc  valiant effort as much as possible.

Recommended weapons: HedgeCutter, Serathil, Ogre Pocket knife.

Follow stat priorities for gear

[enchants]
Follow stat priority. Crusader on weapon

[macros]
stance 1 line, stance 2 tower, stance 3 assault 
Example Macro
#showtooltip Harrowing Melody
/cast [nostance:1] Line Formation
/cast Harrowing Melody
/startattack
------------
#showtooltip Shield of Denial
/cast [nostance:1/2] Tower Formation
/cast Shield of Denial
/startattack
------------------
#showtooltip
/cast Hero's March
/cast Chivalry
/cast Inspiring Presence
/startattack

[tips]
Battle drums can't be clicked while you have a GCD going, and is often not usuable in a raid setting.

entries.title: KOX Hellfire balanced AOE+ST M+ build
entries.description:
[overview]
Great balanced build both for AOE and ST in dungeons and M+

[talents]
Hellstorm is not taken in this build due to it being slightly worse than your usual AOE Demonfire spender Flames of Xoroth and on top of that, there is a great talent to have instead of it which is [Punisher](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:704988) that helps with ST damage, especially while usuing your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300). One of the most powerful AOE in this build is Into the Maw that is used with both [Indiscriminate](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:704958) and [Shadowflame Forge](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:704989) 1/2 in this build which is enough to use [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) 3 times after applying your Hellmaw on your target. This way your Hellmaw spreads on 10 targets total right before exploding with huge damage

[rotation]
Always use your [Pestilence of Apocalypse](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:804786), don't forget to buff Str Mark and call your [Call: Hellfire Imp](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:804883). The Annihilation proc always takes priority to generate Demonfire stacks.
AOE with [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300):
Start with using your [Burning Rage](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:520295) before the pull. Firstly use your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300) and right after that [Unleash Pestilence](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:801002) (try to always refresh it's duration by spending 4+ Demonfire stacks on Flames of Xoroth or Hellmaw) Then use one [Meatsaw](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:501508) to get 6 stacks of Demonfire and right after that apply your Hellmaw on the tankiest target and use enough [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) on your Hellfire target to spread Hellfire on every target that was pulled. If your [Unleash Pestilence](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:801002) is at 1-2 seconds until expiring then use your Flames of Xoroth to refresh it's duration and then continue spreading Hellmaw if needed. After spreading your Hellmaw on every target use Flames of Xoroth and then continue spamming [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) to stack Demonfire if your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300) is still active and spend your Demonfire stacks on Flames of Xoroth if your Hellfire is still up.
AOE when you don't have your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300):
Use your [Meatsaw](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:501508) to gain Demonfire stacks and use them on Hellmaw spreading it 3 times by using your [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) 3 times on CD. In between of using [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) continue using your [Meatsaw](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:501508) to gain Demonfire stacks and Flames of Xoroth to spend your Demonfire stacks if your Hellmaw is still up, othewise use Hellmaw and spread it once again since it still blows up if the target dies dealing more damage than Flames of Xoroth.
ST with [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300):
Start with using your [Burning Rage](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:520295) before the pull. Firstly use your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300) and right after that [Unleash Pestilence](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:801002) (try to always refresh it's duration by spending 4+ Demonfire stacks on Melt, Hellmaw and Skullsplitter) Then spam your [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) with 6 stacks of Demonfire until your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300) ends. After your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300) ends, firstly spend your Demonfire stacks on Melt, then use [Demon Heart](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805669) and apply Hellmaw. Use your Infernal Strike to get Demonfire stacks and cast your [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) at 6 Demonfire stacks when it's not on cooldown before spending your stacks on Skulltaker since [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) deals great damage at 6 Demofire stacks thanks to Brimstone Flames. Try to keep Melt on the target all the time and reapply Hellmaw after the explosion.
ST when you don't have your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300):
Use your Infernal Strike to gain Demonfire stacks and use them on Melt, Hellfire and Skulltaker. Cast your [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) at 6 Demonfire stacks when it's not on cooldown before spending your stacks on Skulltaker since [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) deals great damage at 6 Demofire stacks thanks to Brimstone Flames. Try to keep Melt on the target all the time and reapply Hellmaw after the explosion.

[stats]
I am still not 100% sure about the prio, but imo it's something like this:
Strenght > AP > SP > Int > Stamina (try to get every single item with Strenght, but items with AP and no main stat are also great)
Items with Agility and Spirit are absolutely irrelevant.
As for the secondary stats you should consider getting enough Hit to play comfortably (at least get enough spell hit for now which is not that hard to get with Mythic gear):
Hit > Crit > ARP = Haste
Not sure if ARP or Haste is better for Hellfire, Either way it's better to get Hit or Crit

[gear]
Get yourself 6 pieces of Lightforge set, 2H weapon with either Strenght or AP and other items should be with Strenght. 
As for trinkets there are some really good ones like:
Ramstein's Lightning Bolts
Drakefury Scale
Hand of Justice
Cannonball Runner
Fighter's Seal of Eldre'Thalas
There are also some decent options that, in my opinion, fall slightly short of the trinkets mentioned above:
Draconic Infused Emblem

entries.title: Competitive 1v1 Arena / BG Necromancer PvP Guide
entries.description:
[overview]
Currently, the Animation tree offers the only truly viable spec to compete at a high level in PvP on Conquest of Azeroth. Because of the inherent risk of Necromancer becoming completely overpowered if over-tuned, the class has historically seen heavy tuning. However, with the right setup, Animation offers top-tier minion pressure, control, and explosive burst.

*Abomination and Winds of Northrend are currently dead talents in this build.*

**This build uses 6 Ghouls.**

Currently testing a promising BG version that is outperforming this version in BG.



**For more information on how to become the most imdominatable Necromancer, you can join IMMORTAL Necro-only Guild. 

Lvl 40+
https://discord.gg/rXeQ684Ft**

[talents]
Talent selection varies slightly based on your personal preference, the current meta, and whether you are queuing 1v1 duels or multi-target Battlegrounds.

**Death’s Due:** Less valuable in BGs, but theoretically useful in 1v1s to purge invulnerabilities. However, extensive testing shows it currently fails to reliably purge effects like the Venomancer’s invulnerability. It is recommended to drop this talent until further bug fixes land.

**Gravebound Champion CD Reduction:** Skip this for 1v1s, as rounds end far too fast to get a second cast. It holds much more value in drawn-out BGs.

**Overwhelming Force:** The superior option for baseline Mana and Runic Power generation.

**Phylactery:** Promising on paper, but currently untested in top-tier play and rarely utilized effectively. May be very strong in 2v2 and 3v3. 

**Frost Wyrm Pathing:** Frost Wyrm burst is simply too powerful to pass up. To reach it, you are forced to path through a dead talent: Winds of Northrend (Lichfrost Slow).

**Fetid Ward:** A solid defensive option, though further testing is required to confirm if it outperforms alternative defensive talents.

**Depravity vs. Mindless Fury:** Depravity is currently the stronger pick, though Mindless Fury can be considered if you are heavily stacking Haste.

**Tomb King vs. Bone Wrath:** Tomb King provides significantly higher impact during your primary burst combo.

**Unrelenting:** Turns your Crypt Swarm into a machine gun for Runic Power generation.

[rotation]
## Buffs & Pre-Fight Setup

Minions = 6 Ghouls.


### Baseline Buff Sequence

Keep these active at all times. Use a /castsequence macro to cycle through them quickly before 1v1 rounds or upon spawning in BGs:

Fetid Ward

Greater Grim Mandate

Greater Razorice

Greater Chill of the Tomb

### Combat Stance & Auras

**Assault Stance:** Keep this active continuously for the +5% Critical Strike Chance and increased movement speed for your Ghouls.

**Frozen Reliquary: **Save this for when your Mana pool is completely depleted to maximize the missing-mana scaling benefit.


### Core Opener & Rotation

Pre-Fight Prep: Drop your Summoning Ritual and channel Siphon Mana on your Ghouls to secure an early resources

**Summon Archers:** Always open by summoning your Skeleton Archers. They boost your Haste, deal damage from range, and build early Mana and Runic Power.

**Apply Harvest Plague:** Cast Harvest Plague immediately to begin siphoning health. The DoT tick actively prevents stealth classes from resetting the fight.

**Summon Heavy Minions:** Call forth your Tomb King and Plaguefather.

**Execute the Burst Combo:** Once your opponent commits to the fight and enters melee range of your army or you think you can kill them, pop your macro burst (Unholy Frenzy + Gravebound Champion + Frost Wyrm + Any racial trait) while commanding all ghouls to attack.

[stats]
## Gear & Stat Hierarchy

**Stamina:** Priority #1 for PvP survivability to prevent getting burst down in stun locks.

**Intellect: **Primary stat for raw Spell Power, minion scaling, and Mana pool size.

**Spell Hit Rating:** Mandatory up to the PvP cap (4% / ~32–36 rating at level 60) so crucial CC and burst spells do not miss.

Haste / Critical Strike: Secondary stats to stack based on personal preference (Crit for burst potential, Haste for faster cast cycles).

I've moved away from Crit and have focused on Haste, we can get down to 0.5 sec on a Ghoul summon. Ghouls also go berserk with the extra Haste. [user] much better than crit.

[gear]
Horde/Alliance Insignia for CC cleanse (you can buy this tricket with Honor at the PvP vendor). *This is Goated.*

Main thing is to stop the perma CC from some classes you will face in 1v1.

Always buy PvP gear with honor and start stacking PvP Power to stand a chance. 

Once you are level 60, you can spam BGs and the Call Board Daily for Honor and that will help you get the base PvP needed.

[macros]
Macro I use since it has 3 instant casts that don't trigger global CD and one instant cast that does at the end. 
 
(Unholy Frenzy + Gravebound Champion + Frost Wyrm + Any instant cast racial trait).

Copy and paste the macro below but you will need to remove or replace Arcane Torrent if you are not a Blood Elf:

#showtooltip Animate: Frost Wyrm
/cast Arcane Torrent
/cast Animate: Frost Wyrm
/cast Gravebound Champion
/cast Unholy Frenzy

[tips]
## Utility & Advanced Tactics

**Defensive Tithe Window:** Pop Bone Tithe at around 50% HP. This allows you to stack the shield while maximizing incoming heals from Fetid Ward and Command Attack from Ghouls.

**Gravebound Defensive Offense:** Weave Gravebound Champion into your burst phase to reduce incoming damage while adding another body to your minion army.

**Whenever your attack commands give you a free cast proc:**
Cast Blight if the target still has a large health pool.
Cast Frost Lich to snare fleeing enemies and/or generate a fast burst of Runic Power.

**Runic Power Dumping:** When your Runic Power caps out, spam your Command abilities.

**Minion Recovery:** If your army gets wiped, immediately cast Call of the Grave and resume spamming Ghouls.

### Disruption Control:

**Ghoulify:** Exceptional for catching targets in BGs and interrupting spell casts while your army attacks.

**Mass Grave:** Instant cast at 50+ Runic Power. Serves as a clutch, instant-cast AoE fear to turn the tide when swarmed.

**The "Entomb" Execute Combo:** Entomb an enemy at ~20% health, then instantly follow up with Death's Due. While niche, it provides a flashy execute option.

entries.description:
[overview]
This build focuses more on AoE damage using 5 [Raise: Ghoul](coa-skill:necromancer:500971) and March of the Dead instead of big single target boss damage like my other guide. This build works VERY well with a tank that likes to pull big and preferably LoS the mobs around a corner or against a wall. Also is great for leveling in dungeons if you have people who can do single target damage.

[rotation]
## Opener

- Glacial Ward
- Greater Grim Mandate (Greater Foul Mandate if you already have Grim Mandate from someone else)
- Greater Razorice & Greater Chill of the Tomb (Optional)
- 5 [Raise: Ghoul](coa-skill:necromancer:500971)
- Cap Runic Power with [Glacial Tap](coa-skill:necromancer:805369) or Runic Harvest
**Once tank plants**
- Call of the Grave
- [Animate: Skeletal Archer](coa-skill:necromancer:805040) (Big 25% haste buff)
- [Animate: Bone Wraith](coa-skill:necromancer:805032)
- [Animate: Plaguefather](coa-skill:necromancer:805048)
- [Animate: Frost Wyrm](coa-skill:necromancer:805428)
- [Unholy Frenzy](coa-skill:necromancer:805029)
- March of the Dead (3x)
- [Glacial Tap](coa-skill:necromancer:805369)
- Runic Harvest
- March of the Dead (3x)
(Rinse and Repeat)

entries.title: Animation Necromancer Leveling Guide
entries.description:
[overview]
Still working through this build, open to suggestions. Please comment with any suggestions or questions about the build.

[talents]
10-19: Rush Living Dead and Ghouls taking Bone King over Graverobber to help with early mana issues. 
20-?: From here you have a few options. Rush March of the Dead if you want a MASSIVE AOE ability for big pulls (~5+ targets).... hold off on Lich's Prodigy until you have Overwhelming Force and Lich Commander. Rush OF and LC ASAP to help with mana and RP efficiency. Frozen Reliquary will be a massive help too but may be expensive as corpse dust costs can stack up if you're leaning on it too heavily in the early game. 
Any defensive options shown are lowest priority and strictly taken to fill out the tree and open access to the last 2 talents. 

Decaying Colossus can be swapped for Foul Invocation as both are defensive options. Haven't tested DC against abom but considering he uses a frontal (that we can't aim for him), abom is likely to out perform. 

Unstoppable Frenzy is interchangeable for AotD. UF lines up our Unholy Frenzy with our other 2m CDs for consistent burst phases. AotD would mainly be taken for slightly more mana regen (more minion hits= more mana regen thanks to Overwhelming Force)

[rotation]
Minions
Pre-Ghouls- Abom + 2x warriors
Pre 30- Abom + 2x ghouls
2x crypt fiends works too for 3 targets or less but not a huge difference in damage

Lvl 30+
Abom + 3 Ghouls in virtually all content
2x crypt fiends + 1 ghoul is good for ST but falls behind on mana regen since 3x ghouls + all their talents

Ward - Glacial Ward (Bone Ward until you unlock it)

Mandate - Grim Mandate (Foul Mandate until you unlock it)

Opener
Rune tap right before pull>Call of the Dead> Archers> Tomb King> Plaguefather> Unholy Frenzy> Blood Fury/Berserking (if applicable) begin rotation

Rotation
Blight>Harvest Plague> spam Command Undead if enough RP/Crypt Swarm if not
Archers on CD, Blight on procs ONLY (no hardcast after pull) Lichfrost ONLY IF blight is active on target. DO NOT overwrite blights, the final tick is 25% of the full duration's damage. Rune tap as needed to spam command undead

5+ targets Rotation
Only differences here are to replace command undead with March of the Dead and spam command undead during MotD CD AND spread blight to as many targets as possible with our procs.  10s is a pretty tight window and you typically want to rune tap>MotD every time. This uses a TON of mana, even without Lich's Prodigy. You WILL be drinking/hitting Frozen Reliquary nearly every pull so spam MotD at the risk of your own bank account. 

As of writing this, the wall becomes active roughly 2-3s after casting and marches forward about 20-25 yds. Keep this in mind as these WILL AGGRO mobs so aim carefully. 

Tl;dr- maintain blight/harvest plague on at least one target, crypt swarm- mana efficient RP generator, Runetap- high mana RP generator. Spam Command Undead for free blight/lichfrost procs OR spam MotD to do massive AOE at the cost of corpse dust for Frozen Reliquaries and mana consumables

[stats]
Spell power> Intellect> Stamina.........BUT
we really want a healthy balance of Intellect/Spell power and stamina
Spell power- raw damage
Intellect- mana + crit rating
Stamina- survivability but more importantly, spell damage (15% of your minions' total stamina) yes, your stamina translates to your minions' stamina!
50+, we need to focus on hit rating as well

entries.title: 6 Ghoul Animation
entries.description:
[overview]
Buffs: Grim Mandate, Glacial ward, Razorice, Chill of the Tomb.

We use 6x Ghouls early on and swap to 3x Crypt Fiend for Single target/higher tier contents once bosses start to live longer than 20 seconds. There's a couple of talent changes that come with this build as we no longer need Ghouls when we change.
**You can view that build [Here](https://coabuildhub.com/build/fc8a5133-5ae1-43bc-9855-357f13abdac4)**

We put '/cast Grave March' inside all of our rotational ability macros to stop the zombies from the Unrelenting Army talent being dumb and pulling random packs we aren't in combat with as Grave March is off the GCD. See macro section

Sense Undead gives a 5% damage increase to Undead Mobs. Use it.

[rotation]
You can pre-build Runic Power with Runic Harvest. Do this.

AoE burst Prio: Glacial tap on Cooldown > Blight on 1 Target > March of the Dead > Animations (Tomb King, Skele Archers, Frost Wyrm, Plaguefather) > Unholy Frenzy > Spend excess Runic Power on Command: Undead > Crypt Swarm with Diabolic stacks to generate Runic Power

Single Target Prio: Glacial Tap > Aim for as close to 100% Blight & Harvest Plague uptime > Animations (All) > Unholy Frenzy > Crypt Swarm with Diabolical stacks > Command: Undead > Lichfrost (ONLY WITH BONE KING PROCS) > Death's Due (if boss is 20% or lower)

If you are comfortable with your tank in dungeons, you can utilise Runic Harvest before pulls and early Glacial Taps while the tank is pulling to put up 3/4 Harvest Plague's and a blight while the tank is pulling for some free damage, but you NEED to control these zombies with the macros or they will pull anything and everything.

Get used to using your stances as well, swapping between Assault and Pacify to control your pets. AI is notoriously bad here.

[stats]
Hit to cap > Spell Power > Crit=Haste > Int

[leveling]
Talent Build remains essentially the same while leveling, you swap out Unstoppable Frenzy for Army of the Dead and run 1x Abom, then add Ghouls progressively as you get more Life Force. 
You can swap out Life for Power in the Necromancer talent tree for Command: Hook to help grip mobs in dungeons who may be casting in the distance. 

Abomination provides a 25% attack speed slow to benefit your tank in dungeons, especially powerful until Lv30/40 where non-shield tanks start to gain a lot of their tankiness. 
Run Animate: Bone Wraith until Lv50, then swap to Tomb King.

**Addressing mana issues in the early leveling stages:**
**1.** Create Frozen Reliquary (and Bone Reliquary) are tradeable Health Stones & Mana Potions. **You can make and have more than 1*. As you gain more ranks of the skill, you make more with each cast (Up to a max of 5 per cast at max rank)

**2. **Blight costs a Kidney per cast. Casting 1 of these is expensive, prioritise Bone King procs to Blight uptime, then spend extra on Lichfrost.

**3. **Talent interplay: Overwhelming Force, Animate: Bone Wraith, Forbidden Technique, Graverobber, Skeletal Artillery, Living Dead.
These talents have a lot of interplay to create an alleviation on your mana issues early on, especially when you combine with Frozen Reliquary usage and if you need more you can always add in Mana Potions. 

When you hit Lv60 swap from Abomination & 2x Ghoul, to 6x Ghoul and progress through Normal/Heroic dungeons. Once in Mythic Dungeons and you are comfortable in your ability to not need self-sustain while you learn mechanics you should look at swapping to Crypt Fiend build in the overview.

entries.title: Optimal Build for Raids/M0
entries.description:
[overview]
From testing and discussion amongst other MK players this seems to be the best build available for us for current available content. This is a build purely for level 60 and NOT levelling as Mountain Hammer is near useless in PvE and it is recommended to skip it entirely until 60 whereupon you respec into it to gain Earthen Avatar and Primal Guardian.

[talents]
The only talents I would consider optional and not integral to the build are Boulder Dash and Dreamslip from the Primalist tree, and Bash and Resources of the Earth from the MK tree. However, Replenishment is an extremely valuable asset to bring to a raid and not many classes can take it as easily as we can. If you were to take the point out of Replenishment (if someone in your raid was already providing it) then the best place to put it would be Tilling the Earth for the extra Expertise.

Another option would be to swap out Grove Guardian and/or Protector of the Grove for Earthmother's Blessing if you are worried about getting one shot however if something would kill you on top of the 30% extra health Earthmother's Blessing gives you when it activates - you still die. It is not a cheat death.

Alternatively, if you hate fun, you can swap out Boulder Dash and Environmentalist for Heavy Handed which gives you extra armour on your self heals. This does add yet another buff to keep track of and extra button to press when you're already GCD capped but can make the difference on high damage fights.

[rotation]
Your standard rotation is as follows:

1. Maintain Earth's Rage
2. Reapply Earthquake and Rock Barrier after they end (never before)
3. Keep Quake on cool down and Raging Earth applied
4. Geode Barrage with Aftershock if Earthquake is up
5. Seismic Smash to maintain Thane's Rage and fish for Quake/Aftershock procs
6. Wildclaw as filler

This rotation is pretty much the same for ST and AoE although most AoE situations will involve a lot more EQ opportunities to hold aggro on casters that won't stack or pull more groups.
Seismic abilities **other than Smash** should only be used to pull as they use far too much mana otherwise.
With a fast OH and proper play you should be able to maintain near 100% uptime on Rock Barrier in ST but make sure it falls off before reapplying to refresh Primal Guardian.

Our opener on bosses can be quite complex and some things are not very intuitive so here's an explanation for everything up until your second/third GCD of any given boss encounter. This is made a lot easier to time properly and pull off if you are the one pulling (with a timer).

1. Use Therazane's Rage at least 10s before the fight starts so you begin at max rage. The Primal Fury talent is great here to keep your rage up whilst not in combat
2. Use Rock Barrier 10 seconds before pull. This will make your Primal Guardian trigger at the start of the fight
3. Use Seismic Smash 5-8 seconds before pull to activate Thane's Rage and generate an Aftershock
4. Just Judgement of The Three Hammers just before pull
5. The following abilities, other than the last one, do not use the Global Cooldown (GCD) so should be cast at the same time but in this order: Mountain Avatar > Charge > Earthquake > Quake
6. If you are in Boon of the Bear (which I would recommend on any fight that you know you won't die to) use Primal Convergence, otherwise save it as a defensive ability
7. Proceed with rotation as normal

[stats]
Stat weights are a bit of a meme right now but it's currently understood that Strength/Parry>Stamina>everything else. Nothing deals enough damage to warrant going too tanky and everything you care about scales off of Str/Parry.

[gear]
There has been a lot of discussion on whether we want fast or slow weapons for this spec and I lean heavily into the camp of slow main hand and fast off hand. The argument for having double slow weapons relies on casting Wildclaw often since it scales off of the damage of both weapons. However, Terrasmash, Fury of the Earthmother, and Mountain Avatar make proccing Geodes EXTREMELY beneficial for everything that our spec wants to do. Therefore we want our OH to be as fast as possible to get as many of these off as we can.

The 3 set of Courage you can buy with Marks of Triumph is very nice to have, as well as any Imperial Plate (of Parry) crafted items you can get your hands on otherwise focus on your main stats of Str/Parry.

Here is my current/most recent gear setup for reference:
https://coa.ascensionlogs.gg/armory/James/Rexxar

[enchants]
These are self explanatory; take anything that gives you more of the stats you already want. Double Crusader on weapons.

[macros]
#showtooltip
/startattack
/cast [@cursor] Earthquake
/stopcasting
/cast Therazane's Rage

This is an example of what you want from a macro for this spec.
It is generally a good idea to bind /startattack into all of your main damaging abilities to make sure that you don't lose your target or stop attacking for any reason.
Using the [@cursor] prefix for Earthquake specifically allows you to instantly drop it wherever your mouse is without having to click to confirm the spell. Alternatively, if you're lazy, you can use [@player] to place it on top of yourself.
Adding /stopcasting to your Earthquake and Geode Barrage macros is recommended to avoid accidentally hard casting them whilst tanking as you cannot dodge or parry and whilst casting a spell so will be quickly deleted by whatever mobs are on you.
Also, since Therazane's Rage wants to be cast on cooldown in all situations I would suggest adding it to the macros for your most commonly used spells so it's done automatically and without the need for an extra button press/plate to spin.

#showtooltip
/cancelaura Boulder Dash
/cast Boulder Dash

Missclicking the funny boulder button can get you killed very fast since you cannot mitigate damage during the effect. This macro allows you to instantly cancel it with a second press.

[tips]
Earthquake has some quirks that make it so that you never want to cast it while it's already active as it deals damage through a debuff that is not refreshed by the new instance of the spell on the ground. For this reason you should always wait for your current Earthquake to dissipate before recasting.
Alternatively, in AoE situations, I find liberal usage of Earthquake to pull new packs or keep aggro on stray caster mobs to be extremely beneficial.

While you'll probably spend ~90% of your time tanking in Boon of the Turtle don't forget that other Boons do exist and have their own uses. The dodge chance of Boon of the Wolf (especially under the effects of Primal Convergence) can be stronger than the damage reduction afforded by Turtle in some situations. In other cases where you don't need to be as tanky; Boon of the Bear offers a high damage/threat option. Also, if you've done any amount of dungeon spamming I'm sure you'll have been victim to the amount of fear effects some of them throw at you, in which case Boon of the Lion is surprisingly useful for short bursts of utility.

Another, very niche, quirk that I've found is that Dreamslip seems to be one of the only things that work to drop combat on Captain Kromcrush if you're attempting a Tribute run without the costume.

The extra range of Untamed is not noticeable. 
-Primal Strikes /Primal Fury:  We only take this for pathing. Strikes allows us to generate more Rage during Single target. Primal Fury is simple not needed.
-Protective Roar: very weak, we mostly only use it to get to Therezane´s gift
-Mending Touch /Emerald Will: i´ve found that spending less GCDs on dispelling poisons when there´s multiples is better than the healing but if you dont want Grove Guardian feel free to move this point somewhere else.
-Natural Efficiency: can be a life saver. I dont take it because we are already a bit starved for points but if you really want this take the point from Heavy Handed or Nature´s Call.
-Grove Guardian: When there´s a lot of Poinson or decease this is fantastic, when there isnt then its an ok aoe + healing. If you prefer you can take Earthmother´s Pendant instead.
-Protector of the Grove: Less CD in 2 of our defensive, this is great.  You could take Earthmother´s Blessing instead., so far i haven´t needed it.

Spec Tree:
-Quake: this is just Thunder Clap with a fake moustache. Amazing snap threat
-Mountain Hammer: its quite bad, sometimes it can be used as an interrupt, only take it for pathing.
-Thane´s Guidance: Only pathing, feel free to replace this with Hammer Time! (aoe stun).
-Spiritbound: This gives us infinite rage when fighting multiple enemies and is the core of our strategy (more on that later)
-Bash: sounds great in theory but when taken to the practice... you just dont autoattack that much and this is just RNG. I only take it because its more damage than Hammer time but feel free to take that instead
-Earthen Avatar: Big defensive + Damage Steroid, use it on CD
-Resources of the Earth: Raid buff (Replenishment) and the solution to our mana problems. If someone else is providing this they should probably the ones switching but if they cant for whatever reason then you can take Quakformer for more Quakes.
-Improved Ursoc´s Bellow: is not that good but is far better than Mountain Mover.
-Terrasmash: its here because of the synergy with Fury of the earthmother.
-Earthforged Barrier /Rock Solid: Barrier may be better for raid but as far as M+ go Rock solid is irreplasable. Also the tooltip is a bit unclear, what the talent does is to increase the amount of our Rock barrier from 10 to 15, it doesnt increase the "charges", we dont get 7 Rock barriers to Spam.
-Earthmaker: CDR on Avatar. You can gather multiple packs, Pop Avatar, have your team do big aoe and have avatar again so you can repeat.

[rotation]
Our core gameplay on dungeons is to walk to a pack, use Quake for Snap threat, use Prima Rush towards the next pack and ether use our second charge of quake or Earthquake Proc if available.
If we already Quake is on CD and we want more mobs we may need to use Bearclaw to fish for an Aftershock for the Free Earthquake.
Once all enemies are gathered we mostly keep an Earthquake active, we use Quake on CD and we spam heals, your rage shoulnt spend more than a second bellow cap.
Once most mobs are dead and we are just finishing the ones still alive we can focus more on bearclaw, the damage is trash but the double hit means CDR for avatar. Also you still want to maintain Earthquake but if you get aftershocks back to back you should use the second on Geode Barrage.

entries.title: Flameweaving: The Phoenix Healer
entries.description:
[overview]
🎵 🔥🔥 [Pyromania - Cascada](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EsdXPPp8dNk) 🔥🔥 🎵

Flameweaving transforms our destructive fire magic into a force of restoration. While its core toolkit excels at sustained single-target healing, the specialization truly shines through its versatile and engaging resource management. As we heal and deal damage, we generate **Embers** - a secondary resource that fuels a variety of powerful and flexible abilities. Whether we need burst healing, team shielding, or extra damage, smart Ember management gives us the flexibility to adapt to every encounter.

You'll love the Flameweaving Pyromancer if you enjoy:

- **FIRE EVERYWHERE**
- Having a Phoenix pet
- Nearly infinite mana
- Secondary resource management
- Weaving damage into your healing rotation

[rotation]
**Mana**

You'll rarely need to worry about mana after level 30 thanks to a combination of different passives and buffs.

- **[Ashen Priest](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=707432)** maintains 20% of your mana regeneration while in combat while also granting **[Replenishment](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=1257670)** whenever you critically heal, restoring 5% mana to yourself and your party.

- **[Ashen Skin](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=504720)** increases your in-combat mana regeneration by an additional 60%.

- **[Shazzrah's Boon](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=807126)** restores 2% of your total mana whenever you spend an Ember, providing excellent passive sustain alongside **[Seal of Al'ar](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=808012)**, a buff we can apply to ourselves and others which restores mana every 5 seconds.

If you or a teammate ever begins running low on mana, **[Essence of Malygos](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=802120)** restores 36% of total mana over 9 seconds.

---

**Core Abilities & Gameplay**

Flameweaving isn't built around a rigid rotation. Instead, success comes from understanding your toolkit and maintaining enough Embers to flex into whatever the situation requires.

Nearly every healing or damage spell that **doesn't consume an Ember** generates Heat.

**100 Heat = 1 Ember**

Throughout this guide, abilities that consume an Ember are marked with 🔥.

---

**Mana Only**

**Phoenix Pet -** **[Phoenix Egg](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=800796)**

Your Phoenix should be active at all times. It lasts 60 seconds and pulses light AoE healing every 5 seconds (3 seconds with this build). Beyond its healing, several of your abilities require your Phoenix to be active.

*See the **Tips** section for the WeakAura I use to track its duration and prevent it from expiring during important moments.*

**Emergency Cooldown(2 Mins) -** **[Kael's Command](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=800816)**

Requires your Phoenix to be active. For 10 seconds, your Phoenix pulses powerful AoE healing, making this your strongest answer when multiple party members begin dropping quickly. Don't be afraid to use it proactively during heavy group-wide damage.

**Fast Heal -** **[Kindle](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=803825)**

A quick, medium-strength heal with no Ember cost.

**Slow Heal -** **[Cinderheart](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=502052)**

A slower but significantly larger heal with no Ember cost.

**Shield -** **[Inferno Barrier](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=535651)**

An instant single-target shield with a short cooldown. Best applied to the tank between pulls rather than during heavy combat.

**AoE Damage / Healing -** **[Cleansing Flames](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=681374)**

**Our bread and butter.** This spell does an incredible amount of heavy lifting by dealing moderate damage while simultaneously healing and shielding allies in a cone.

Don't let the small visual effect fool you - the cone is far more generous than it appears. Position yourself to hit enemies while simultaneously healing and shielding your tank and nearby allies.

**Large AoE Damage -** **[Meteor](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=500652)**

An instant-cast AoE with a cooldown. Drop this into large enemy packs before beginning your Cleansing Flames spam.

**Ember Generator -** **[Lava Shard](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=503239)**

An instant-cast ranged nuke with a 10 second cooldown that immediately generates **1 Ember**.

Use this on cooldown whenever you aren't Ember capped. If you're already sitting at maximum Embers, hold it until you've spent one to avoid wasting generation.

*See the **Tips** section for a basic WeakAura cooldown tracker if you'd like one.*
---

**🔥 Ember Spenders**

**High Priority**

**🔥 Instant Heal -** **[Ember Touch](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=520320)**

An instant medium-strength heal with no cooldown. Excellent for saving fragile party members when there's no time to cast Kindle, or whenever you have Embers to spare. Use this liberally.

**🔥 Group Shield -** **[Phoenix Dive](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=706854)**

An instant AoE shield with no cooldown.

Use this frequently between pulls or whenever you have excess Embers to cushion incoming damage before it happens. It shields allies in a medium-sized area around your target and requires your Phoenix to be active.

**Lower Priority**

**🔥 Single Target Damage -** **[Explode](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=502060)**

Decent nuke if you have excess embers and literally nothing else to do.

**🔥 Damage over Time -** **[Blaze](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=534604)**

Keep this on bosses if healing is under control and you have spare Embers.

**🔥 Line Damage / Healing -** **[Ignis Ultimatus](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=280570)**

My class talent capstone of choice. After a short cast, unleash a massive line of fire that deals heavy damage to enemies while simultaneously providing moderate healing to allies caught in its path.

While it's generally not worth spending an Ember on cooldown, it becomes an excellent choice whenever your positioning allows you to hit several enemies while also healing multiple allies. Think of it as a more powerful version of Cleansing Flames that looks badass.

**🔥 Multi-Target Damage -** **[Flames of Neltharion](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=535512)**

Hits your target and two nearby enemies.

In practice, it's usually better to be casting Cleansing Flames or almost anything else, making it a very low-priority Ember spender.

---

**Typical Pull Strategy**

Before each pull:

- 🔥 Apply **Phoenix Dive** to shield the group before encounters.
- Refresh **Phoenix Egg** if necessary.
- Apply **Inferno Barrier** to the tank if you can spare the global cooldown.

Once combat begins:

- Open with **Meteor** against large packs.
- Position yourself so **Cleansing Flames** strikes enemies while covering the tank and as many party members as possible.
- In easier content, Cleansing Flames alone will often handle the majority of your healing.
- When heavy group damage is incoming, activate **Kael's Command** to stabilize the party.
- As incoming damage increases, spend Embers aggressively on **🔥 Ember Touch** and **🔥 Phoenix Dive** to stabilize the group.

[stats]
Spirit + Crit are your core priorities.  Anything else is gravy.

Critical heals give us many synergies like mana regeneration and free shields.

my current pyro dps raid profile which doesn't use any of the last three talent nodes because i think they are not that good

[talents]
you can swap 1 explosive point for Rapid Incineration to get more Lava Shards which results in getting more ember stacks but idk its lowkey not good

[rotation]
Get 5 ember stacks before pull

On pull cast Ignite -> Blaze -> Lava Shard 

Now if your tank is not good at keeping threat at the start just keep spamming Flare Bolt or a Meteor untill he builds up some threat . if he is good on threat start Blasting

Pop Fired Up! and Eruption and your trinkets . Start spamming Explode
keep an eye out for your ember stacks . if its getting lower than 3 stacks cast a lava Shard between Explodes to get embers . refresh Blaze if it ran out .
if you ever run out of embers while Fired Up! unlucky i guess blame rng and cast a few flare bolts to get 1 ember and back to spamming explode

After Fired Up! expire reapply all your dots and spam Flare Bolt untill you reach 5 ember stacks then spam explode until you reach 0 ember stacks . keep an eye out for Fired Up! because you need to have 5 ember stacks when it comes off cooldown.


if there are more than 1 target use Flames Of Neltharion instead of explode

[stats]
crit and haste can make your Fired Up! last longer which means more dps . so i guess


Hit Rating until cap-> Spell Power -> Crit -> Haste -> Int -> Spirit

[tips]
basically 95% of your damage comes when you have Fired Up! active so use your trinkets and Eruption Only while its active .

entries.title: Incineration - Explode ST build
entries.description:
[overview]
The build is focused on high single target damage and relies heavily on consecutive burst windows by building up full ember stacks and using [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823) to spend and extend as much as possible, by using [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792).

**Please note that this guide is being continuously updated according to the changelog and optimal DPS results in raid environment. After the raid comes out - we will have better examples for numbers.**

*I am currently investigating if Pyroclastic Flow and [Flames of the Firelord](coa-skill:pyromancer:800819) are better than Heat Wave and Sulfuron Harbringer. As well as other talent combinations*

[talents]
The key talents around this build are [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823) and Sulfuron Harbringer.
The goal is to have very high burst single target windows, by spamming as much [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792) as possible and extending the duration of [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823).
As all the global cooldowns and casting time will be primarily taken by spamming [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792), the additional damage amplification will come passively from the burning DoTs and Sulfuron Harbringer.
The idea for taking Sulfuron Harbringer instead of Pyroclastic Flow is simply because of the extended duration of [Blaze](coa-skill:pyromancer:534600) - During burst, you still have your [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823) and embers, but your DoTs run out, which reduces your damage quite a lot.

[rotation]
**General rule of thumb:**
## 1. DoTs always need to be on the target, as they generate Heat and deal damage, as well as proc Sulfur Flames from Sulfuron Harbringer.
 - [Ignite](coa-skill:pyromancer:502020)
 - [Blaze](coa-skill:pyromancer:534600)
 - [Lava Shard](coa-skill:pyromancer:503231) (Infernus passive)
 - [Scorched](coa-skill:pyromancer:704801) (Passive from direct critical strikes from Ember spenders like [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792))

## 2. Embers always need to be 3+(full before activating [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823)
 
### - If [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823) is on cooldown follow this logic:
  - Less than 3 embers - use [Flare Bolt](coa-skill:pyromancer:502011)
  - More than 3 embers - use [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792)
 
### - If [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823) is active follow this logic:
  - Spam [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792) until you run out of embers
  - If no embers are available, use [Meteor](coa-skill:pyromancer:500135) & [Lava Shard](coa-skill:pyromancer:503231) or [Flare Bolt](coa-skill:pyromancer:502011) until enough for [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792).


## 3. [Meteor](coa-skill:pyromancer:500135) should be always used on cooldown.


## 4. Eruption should always be used together with [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823) and racials, trinkets, etc.



***Burst window opener with full cooldowns and buffs(full ember stacks before pull):***
1. Start with [Ignite](coa-skill:pyromancer:502020)on the Target
2. Apply [Blaze](coa-skill:pyromancer:534600)
3. Cast [Lava Shard](coa-skill:pyromancer:503231)
4. Cast [Meteor](coa-skill:pyromancer:500135)
5. Pop all cooldowns, buffs. - Eruption, [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823), Racial spell, Trinket, Potions
6. Start spamming [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792)
7. If you run out of Embers - cast [Lava Shard](coa-skill:pyromancer:503231) and then continue with [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792)
8. If [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823) is still active and has some time left and [Lava Shard](coa-skill:pyromancer:503231) is on cooldown - Use [Flare Bolt](coa-skill:pyromancer:502011) until enough for [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792) **or** re-apply your dots: [Ignite](coa-skill:pyromancer:502020), [Blaze](coa-skill:pyromancer:534600).

[stats]
Hit cap(17%) > Spell power > Critical > Intellect > Haste > Spirit > Stamina
High critical items needed, as you need to crit as much as possible during Fired Up!

[gear]
[Pre-Raid BIS](https://coa.bisbeard.com/b/Xz1JNB018tjKA-) (17% hit capped)
Items with high spell power, hit, critical and intellect

[enchants]
check this [Pre-Raid BIS](https://coa.bisbeard.com/b/Xz1JNB018tjKA-) guide
