[talents]
Warpdagger does not have a GCD and can be used after breaking stealth with Runic Breakout, or after Hurricane with Waveforged to not incur a cooldown with the Shroudwalker talent. The damage and Smolder resets are valuable to get big dam out and bait cooldowns.

[rotation]
Dagger in stealth for damage amp. Palm Sigils and Zenith before big dam. Silences can't be trinketed so that has a lot more value then it may initially seem. Warp dagger cancel macro for extra smolders, or go in to Hurricane which usually forces something 95% of the time unless they're a Felsworn player or something. 

Use Cinderwake against classes that have a vanish so they can't get away from you. More experience players will vanish during your Hurricane, but with Cinderwake it will continue tracking them.

[stats]
Agility > Stamina > Intellect > Strength > Spirit. Intellect is our only source of maximum mana but Agility and Stamina are too important. Intellect is moreso just a nice stat to have if it so happens to fit in with everything else. 

Attack Power is highly valuable. However, with the way Riftblade scales with Agility, having Agility on your gear will be more beneficial than attack power.

[gear]
Druid 2 set legs and gauntlets. Rogue 4 set Helm, shoulders, chest, and boots. 6 set bonuses are useless so you get the extra 20 resil instead with some intellect sprinkled in. Polearm of course as main weapon, this should be your first conquest buy. Wand because there's no throwing weapon so this is the only option. Stam, int, and some spell pen ain't bad though.

Wrists: Bloodforged Malefic Bracers

Belt: Bloodforged Belt of the Trickster

Both these wrists and belt give expertise so they're highly valuable and pretty expensive usually. With +8 expertise enchant on chest and full conquest gear you will just be able to hit 26/26 expertise cap.

[enchants]
Strider on weapon. +8 expertise (magescale gambeson) on chest. Agi, Agi/Stam, or Atk power/Stam/Resil on everything else. 

Belt and wand have enchants you can put on them as well but it is costly. Belt enchant gives agi so that takes prio over want imo

[leveling]
Not the best leveling class but you'll be ok just gl hf.

[pvp]
Typically you want a way out with Echo Rune or Warpdagger most of the time. Arcane Sigil silence cannot be trinketed and in many cases is a stronger opener than Earth. Look to setup Smolders with Hoarfrost freeze procs and Ice Rune for big burst damage (this is pretty important for closing out kills actually). 

Use cancelaura warpdagger macro to spam that shit after a stealth engage for guaranteed smolder resets when you're going for the kill on someone. Make sure they're frozen!

Primordial Fury has niche case, but important use cases. Felsworn spamming manasteal on you is a big one, primordial with water tattoos will help you with that. Using it with Air tattoos for 40% MS and 40% chance to resists snares is a good gap closer. Crit damage if you're going for the kill but I dont use this often as I usually lose track due to the mental load of pvp and run out of mana.

[macros]
I made simple macros and named every Palm Sigil and Weapon Engraving ability (ex: Palm SIgil: Frost macro is named Slow) because it's hard to see what these abilities do at a glance, since they share similiar artwork with all the other engraving and palm sigils. 

I also macro Zenith to whatever my current on-use trinket is for simplicity (not your PvP Insignia trinket ofc).

#showtooltip Glacial Rune
/cast [@cursor] Glacial Rune

Macro to cancel warpdagger so you can use it again without warping. The daggers stay but it makes things confusing as to where you'll exactly warp to if you throw them willy nilly. 

#showtooltip Warpdagger
/cancelaura warp
/cast warpdagger

[tips]
Granite Resolve is a 1 minute cooldown 40% DR that can be used in stuns. Don't be afraid to press it if you're scared of incoming damage. Make sure you have a way out with Echo Rune or Warpdagger in most cases, unless you know you'll be winning the fight, and/or need to give chase. Keep track of abilities that cost a lot of mana since using these willy-nilly will run you OOM in no time. Riftblade has major mana problems atm and it's hard to make use of utility, you basically need to be in Water tattoo stance 95% of the time.

entries.title: Moon Guard Tank
entries.description:
[overview]
This is meant to be a quick and simple guide, only highlighting the most important talents and skills

[talents]
Class Tree:
-Touch of Moonlight: at first sight this may seem the same like Moonlight Splash but it scales a lot better
-Infused Aegis: since all Aegis share CD you will never use this, only in tree becasue it comes with the spec.
-Aspect of the Cosmos: We use this 99% of the time, there are a few talents that buff Aspect of the stars but its not worth ever using them so Cosmos is our only option.... Huntress can be used in niche situations tho.
-Lunar Lance/ Moonlit Lancer: we only use Lunar Lance on St situations and in those situations we tendo to use it often so we never get value from the 20s DoT.
-Vial of Moonwell Water: Stuns can be lethal so having a way to counter them is great (hope you can react quickly.
-Starshatter: Nice Stun in a long-ish line, keep in mind theres a bit of a delay before the stun takes effect.
-Moonblessed Aspets: you can get up to 78% slow semi permanently, helps a lot with kiting
-Elune´s Presence: in my experience effects like this are trash

Spec Tree:
-Starburst: Use on CD on AoE for uncapped damage and to apply Scattered Stars on AoE wich will then synergice with other stuff
-Blanket of Stars: Our bread, we constantly switch between this and Celestial Aegis, we only spend 1-2s without one or the other.
-Astral Reconstitution: This is terrible, we dont really use it in normal combat, only maybe right after reviving, its here for pathing
-Shrouded Stars: 3%DR aura, if someone else has it you should tell them they can switch, we dont have use for the talent 2 points
-Pulsar Explosion: Sounds good the problem is Celestial Cleaves deals no damage and the Scattered start it could apply is RNG thus inconsistent thus bad
-Blade of the Moon: Helps a lot on Single target and is nice to have something that adds variety to our gameplay.
-Coalesced Resilience: Surpricingly good, we are the kind of tank that pulls defensiveness from every single source possible so even if flat DRs tend to not be that good the fact that we are supporting it with everything else makes it a nice addition. Honestly you can take whatever from the bottom 6 talents, they are all great except for Mooncharged Blades.
-Moon Charged Blades: Mid AF in a tier where all other talens are amazing.
-Chosen of the moon: Big defensive + AoE taunt, what else could a tank desire?

[rotation]
I usually dont say much about rotation but Moon Guard is a particularly tricky tank, Weakauras are kinda necesary or you will die.
We want to pop our Celestial Aegis when starting to collect mobs, ideally you want to track it with a weakaura. When Aegis ends all mobs should be already gathered and you need to pop Blanket of Stars, by the time Blanket ends Aegis will only have 1-2s CD left, this is when you need to be most aware about your HP. use Lunar Eclipse + Touch of Moonlight to heal and/or kite (that 78% slow from Aspect of the Cosmos comes real handy here). Also try to maintain Eclipse of Fury, that´s the defensive part of out gameplay...

For Single Target you want to use Moonblade on Proc and spam Starsunder until you have 5-6 Stacks of Starshatter, then use Celestial Lance and start spamming Starsunder again. Your "consume scattered stars" effect works in a "train effect" it consumes one stack then another and another until there are no more stacks so you can keep spamming starsunder, eventually the train effect will stop but by that time you used a single Star Lance to consume some 8-12 stars. Dont Forget to weave Moonblade procs when they occur.

For AoE what we wanna do is to use Starburst -> Celestial Cleve once if there are not many mobs (3-6) -> Starsweep. This should mass pop your Scattered Stars giving you all the CD from both Starsweep and Starbrust allawing you to repeat. 
If somehow you hit 0 Mana then use Celestial Strike to recover.
A Problem you may have is Snap threat... we dont have it, Celestial Cleave´s damage is pitiful and the skill itself is a cone so its hard to hit mbs that are just a bit separated. You should communicate with your team and let them know you need a bit of time to get your ball roling

[gear]
Ideally we want Tank Plate armor with both Strenght, Intelligence and Stamina
Our second option are Tank Plate armor with Strenght and Stamina
Our Third option are Tank Plate armor with Int and Sta.

[overview]
# 🏹 Ascension Cosmic Hunter/Healer Rotation Guide 🌕

Welcome to the ultimate performance breakdown for the high-tempo **Moon Priest** build. This hybrid specialization focuses on generating **Scattered Stars** resources and detonating them via **Lunar Eclipse** windows for explosive raid healing or infinite mana sustain.

---

### 🔄 Core Single-Target & Boss Priority

The heart of this build revolves around a simple, high-velocity loop: **Build to 6 stacks, modify your state, and detonate.**

#### 1️⃣ The Stack Engine (Building Power)
* **`Huntress Shot` (Spam Filler):** Your primary baseline activity. Chain this **4 to 6 times** sequentially. 
* ⚠️ *Pro-Tip:* Resist the urge to pop your stars early! Maximizing your stacks to the cap of 6 ensures perfect global cooldown (GCD) efficiency and peak throughput.

#### 2️⃣ The Cosmic Payoff (Unleashing the Stars)
When you hit max stacks, or the raid takes a sudden chunk of damage, execute the burst engine:
* 💎 `Lunar Eclipse` ➔ 🌊 `Moonflow`
* *Why it works:* `Lunar Eclipse` completely resets and removes the cooldown of `Moonflow`. This allows you to instantly detonate your accumulated Scattered Stars for a massive tidal wave of raid healing without dropping a global.

#### 3️⃣ Tank Maintenance
* **`Touch of Moonlight`:** Your main priority is keeping *Eclipsing Arrow* active on the active tank at all times.
* *The Trick:* Always activate `Lunar Eclipse` first to turn `Touch of Moonlight` into an **instant cast**, preventing any downtime on your DPS/Healing rotation.

#### 4️⃣ The Mana Recovery Loop 🔋
If your mana pool starts dipping, immediately shift from a healing priority to a sustain priority:
* **Weave `Moon Arrow` (Rank 2):** Swap your filler from Huntress Shot to Moon Arrow. The Rank 2 variant features a hyper-short cast time, allowing you to regen mana without stalling your momentum.
* **The Mana Dump:** Instead of detonating your Scattered Stars with Moonflow, pop them using **`Lunar Lance`** to aggressively restore your mana bar.

---

### ⚡ Major Cooldown Management

| Cooldown | Icon/Combo | Optimal Usage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stellar Convergence** | 🌌 | Cast 2–3 seconds *before* a massive, scripted boss AOE mechanic hits the platform. |
| **Moonwell** | 🔮 | Drop immediately after *Stellar Convergence*. Use the mana replenishment to spam instant-cast heals during the high-stress Full Moon window. |

---

### 💥 AOE & Trash Pull Automation

When the tank grabs massive packs of trash, your job is to turn enemy mobs into healing beacons for your party.

1.  🛡️ **Protect:** Ensure the tank is pre-buffed with *Eclipsing Arrow* (`Lunar Eclipse` ➔ `Touch of Moonlight`).
2.  🌱 **Seed:** Wait for the pack to cluster tightly, then drop **`Starshatter`**. This locks the pack down with a group stun and instantly paints **Scattered Stars** onto *every single enemy* in the pull.
3.  💥 **Detonate:** Immediately unleash **`Lunar Eclipse` ➔ `Moonflow`**. Detonating Scattered Stars across a massive clump of enemies simultaneously produces an unparalleled amount of localized AOE healing.

entries.description:
[overview]
Stance Dancing allows you to keep up with most DPS - especially after you add in Blessing of Absolution to your own dps !

This is a faster paced playstyle if you want to do as much dps as possible while providing your groups with a ton of healing.

[talents]
Change out Sanctified, and Faith for Everglow, and Sunbeams for Raids.

I don't think Cultivate Divinity + Empowered Holy Form is worth it because you'll probably not be casting Illumination a lot.

With more Haste - Gateway to Heaven becomes more attractive than Blazing Chariot - then your whole goal is to get in and out of Dawn as fast as possible. Though if you prefer a slightly slower playstyle then Blazing Chariot is still great !

You can take Unbreakable Focus, Suncharged (it does ~5% of your damage in dungeons), or Gleaming Vigil. 
I'm going with Unbreakable Focus combined with Final Vows, and Heaven's Appraisal it will allow you to get back into Vow of Dawn spam quicker. 

Enveloped in Light is a PvP talent since you're not going to be wearing much Mail and Plate at 60.

[rotation]
You'll want to be stance dancing as much as possible ! 

Solar Invocation: Conquest should be used on cooldown, and I think it's optimal to Radiant Conversion every time you're below ~85% mana. 

The rotation should be something like: 

Vow of Grace to build Solar Power -> Vow of Dawn + Dawn -> Sunflare / Heals -> Radiant Conversion + Conquest -> Vow of Grace -> Repeat

Your goal isn't to use all your stacks, but to maintain your mana as much as possible to keep spamming Sunflares inside of Vow of Dawn. Stance dancing, and using Radiant Conversion early with Conquest will allow you to get back into Dawn quickly. 

You rarely ever want to be building your own Solar Power, and that's why you always want to rely on Vow of Grace.

Vow of Grace and Vow of Dawn are the bread and butter, while Vow of Radiance should be used for the Dawn effect situationally - boss damage when you're not regenning, or to pump out massive heals when pulls go wrong.

Once you've picked up Dawnfall you can swap to Vow of Grace to get full mana every time you use Dawnfall. You can even wait for the last ~5 seconds, or as mobs are beginning to die to swap to Grace. 

Stand in melee to get as much Gavel of Grace, Judgement Day, and Radiance off as possible.

-

Once you get higher haste or two points into Guiding Glow - 

You can begin to cycle through Dawns very quickly for Gateway to Heaven: 

Start in Vow of Grace → Vow of Dawn + Dawn → 3-6 casts → Conquest + Radiant Conversion → 1-2 casts → Dawn again → 3-6 casts -> Radiant Conversion + Vow of Grace for 3-5 seconds -> Vow of Dawn + Dawn -> Repeat

When you have Conquest off cooldown stay in Vow of Dawn and Radiant Conversion at 10 or 9 stacks, or when Radiance ends - whichever happens first. 

It should be optimal to drop Dawn at any time around 10-8 stacks.

[gear]
This is the gear I'll be going for once I hit 60: https://coa.bisbeard.com/b/9Zegnfw8udGPVt

Haste should be incredibly bonkers to get in and out of Dawn or use its stacks, and to cast Sunflares faster

-

Alternatively: You can start playing with Gateway to Heaven early by putting two points into Guiding Glow, then begin to rush Final Vows -> Unbreakable Focus. You can put a point into Suncharged until Unbreakable Focus opens up too.

entries.title: PVE Crusader Templar
entries.description:
[overview]
Thoughts on the Templar Crusader: It's tanky and can deal insane damage at the same time because of crit. Not to mention, it can sustain itself with little to no healing from a dedicated healer.  However, it's a combo oriented class, and a misclick can mean the very end of you. Also, gears are hard to come by since mail armor is a traditionally STR-STA stat gear. However, once you optimize your gear, you'll have a fun time watching mobs fall to you.

For combo build up (your oaths):
This build only relies on combo skills, Righteous Lunge and Cleave. Lunge gives you a 10% additional damage and healing for each stack. Cleave on the other hand allows you to hit an additional enemy for each stack. Now it is important to remember that Cleave stacks only affect combo finishers and other damage-dealing skills that do not rely on oaths (cleave into lunge doesn't give you 2 lunge stacks).

Main Damage Skills:
Our main damage comes from Righteous Tempest, Argent Blade, Scarlet Hammer and Titanstrike.
Righteous Tempest - aoe damage (but also useful for single dps), draw mobs in with threat and mini black hole (if you know Dota 2) from Templar Rituals spec
Argent Blade - crit damge and health sustain
Scarlet Hammer - damage and energy sustain
Titanstrike - finisher damage due to high crit chance  (Judgment of the Gods spec) and health sustain

It is important to note that Tempest is our only combo finisher skill. This is why it is important to reset your oaths every time Tempest is used. It is equally worth noting that Tempest (as well as other combo finisher skill), relies on the actual number of oaths active, not the number of different kinds of oaths active (3 stacks of Cleave deals the same Tempest damage as a Cleave, a Lunge and a Condemn active). That is why it only important to only use Lunge and Cleave to maximize damage while maintaining energy efficiency.

**For rotations, see Rotations tab**

[rotation]
Rotations would only depend if it's single target DPS or AOE DPS

For single target:

Opener:
Lunge -> Lunge -> Tempest

If Argent Blade procs:
Lunge -> Lunge -> Argent Blade -> Scarlet Hammer -> repeat AB-SH if it is still proc-ing, otherwise go Tempest

If Argent Blade does not proc:
Lunge -> Lunge -> Argent Blade -> Scarlet Hammer (if SH procs)
Lunge -> Lunge -> Argent Blade -> Tempest

This is not a strict formula because we want to use AB-SH combo as much as possible when AB procs. In fact, use AB-BH everytime it procs as long as you have a Lunge or 2 active.

Finisher (Titanstrike available):
Lunge -> Lunge -> Titanstrike (skip lunges if there are oaths still active) -> AB-SH (if it procs and repeat if AB procs after SH use until AB no longer procs), otherwise use Tempest -> Lunge -> Titanstrike (off cooldown)

For multiple targets:

Opener:
Lunge -> Lunge -> Tempest

If Argent Blade procs:
Lunge -> Cleave (1-2 times depending if two or more than 3 mobs) -> Argent Blade -> Scarlet Hammer -> repeat AB-SH combo as long as AB still procs -> Tempest

If Argent Blade does not proc:
Lunge -> Cleave (1-2 times depending if two or more than 3 mobs) -> Argent Blade -> Scarlet Hammer (if it procs) -> Tempest
Lunge -> Cleave (1-2 times depending if two or more than 3 mobs) -> Argent Blade -> Tempest

Finisher (Titanstrike available):
Lunge -> Cleave (1-2 times depending if two or more than 3 mobs) -> Titanstrike (skip oaths if oaths still active) -> AB-SH (if it procs), otherwise use Tempest -> Titanstrike (off cooldown)

Like with single-target DPS, we want to use and abuse AB-SH combo and keep hitting AB-SH to multiple enemies until AB no longer procs and then go Tempest.

Why only 2-3 oaths?
In theory, I'm not thinking about damage dealing (you have a high crit rate, the damage comes naturally) but enemy damage mitigation, energy management and health sustain with skills and their respective specs. Enemies will eventually fall but we have to stay alive and be able to have the energy to use our skills, especially if you're just solo-ing.

Why only 1-2 Cleave stacks?
Same reason as above. You'll have to also prioritize staying alive for solo runs.

How about reaching your target?
Unfortunately, we only have Divine Force and Silverhand Incantation as gap-closers. Use them if available before opening with Lunge.

[overview]

This is my current Venomancer Tank build.

You can only use two vemon's at once. As a tank you'll use Weakening Venom and Blight Venom.
- Weakening Venom ( 35% chance to deal 80 shadow damage and reduce the enemy's attack power by 241 for 12 sec)
- Blight Venom ( 30% chance to poison an enemy dealing 1852 shadow damage over 9 sec)

You have a choice to use Greater Spider Pheromones (+92 Agil) or Greater Beetle Pheromones ( + Armor 343 and all primary stats by 14). For mythics, I just use spider pheromones as you get more attack power, 3crit hit, increased armor, and increased Dodge chance.


#1- In the Class tree- when picking talents do not pick Shadra's Lair. As a tank when you use Burrow or the Lair you lose agro and the mobs go straight to the highest threat which is normally the healer.  The only reason to use this is to hide from a big one-shot boss ability. I picked up burrow only because I didn't see another useful talent to pick.

#2- In the class tree - I picked Chitinous Spikes over the only other viable pick which is Venomizer.  With Venomizer I don't have any issues with my current proc chance, so I'm thinking the extra reflective damage is best for threat and dps.

#3- In the Fortitude Tree pick Impale, this is not only useful but I find it fun to position the mobs in a line and then impale them. It does a ton of damage and stuns the mobs, bonus it looks cool.

#4- In the Fortitdue tree- although the Barbed stinger looks good, I don't find it useful enough to waste a talent point on it. I do have 1 point in wicked barbs because it applies Wicked poison when you use Chitin Rush which i use when it is up.

[talents]
I explained in the overview but here are my key points.

On the Fortitude Tree:
1- I only used 1 point in Vile Fury because I'm already over the hit cap and with all the big pulls I'm rarely starved for rage so I chose to put the other point elsewhere.
2- I picked Pendo's Charm over Catalyst because your dots are always doing damage and filling your rage.
3- I picked Slimy Stingers over Slimy because you should be constantly using Carapace Crash to generate threat and DPS. There is no cooldown so every time you hit Carapace Crash and hit an enemy it puts a poison pool on the ground.
4-I picked Chitinous Surge over Empowered Exoskeleton because the reduced Cooldown and increased DPS is better than a 5-yard range increase.
5- I picked Impale because it's my favorite skill and extremely useful. You can use it to do a ton of AOE damage or another interrupt.

For the Venomancer Tree:
#1 -Never pick Shadra's Lair- completely useless for a tank. When you use those all the agro goes to whoever is next on the threat meter, which could be the healer... Burrow is similar but I picked it last because there wasn't a better talent to take. Burrow is very situational, hiding for a boss's one-shot mechanic. I haven't yet find a useful use for burrow but maybe for raids.
#2- Pick up Lifeblood, you will use this for the 20% damage deduction. I use this all the time in big pulls.
#3- Pick up Tome of Ahn"Kahet- This procs all the time, giving you a free attack.
#4- I had one point left over, so I picked Adrenal Venom. I'm still testing this out but normally I use Weakening Venom and Blight Venom.

[rotation]
Pull: Use Hive Instinct if you have no rage.
Chitin Rush, Carapace Crash, Claw Strike, Venomtip Poison, Carapace Regeneration

When your rage gets low, use Claw Strike. As long as you never run out of range, your Carapace Regeneration will stay active. Best practice is to never get to 3 stacks as it drains rage 10 rage every second per stack. 1 stack only 10 rage per second, which is easy to maintain. 3 stacks is 30 rage per second, and you'll be empty before you know it. For big AOE groups, you can stack to 2, and you should be good.

Line up the mobs and use Impale.

Use Chitin rush to do more damage and threat. Be careful not to agro another group or use it to get more mobs to tank,

Use vile sting whenever it is up. This is a free Venom trigger.

If you have no health concerns, use expulsion for extra DPS. If your healer is having issues keeping you topped off, then save your stacks of exposed flesh for your defensive cooldowns.

If you run out of rage, hit Hive Instinct for 100 rage (2 min cooldown)

If your health starts to drop use use your Defensive Cooldown
- if you have high exposed flesh stack use Regrow Exoskeleton - reduce damage by 20% and an additional 1 sec per stack.
- if below 50% use Harden- reduce damage by 45%, decaying quickly over 10 sec and healing for 1% maximum health each time a stack is removed(3 minute cooldown)
- Use lifeblood- reduce damage 20%. 
Try to alternate your defensive cooldowns; try not to blow them all at once.

For spell interruption, you have two options:
1- Nullifying Toxin (16 sec cooldown)
2- Impale (40 sec cooldown )

[stats]
Stamina>Agility>Attack power>Spell Power>Intel

Stamina gives you Health and increases the damage of Claw Strike. The key to this build is stacking Stamina. When you use Carapace Regeneration, that means you restore 1% of maximum health every 1 sec. The more health, the more regeneration. For example, I'm at around 12K health right now. When I have 2 stacks of Carapace regeneration up then I'm healing myself 240 health per sec. 

Agility gives you attack power, Critical hit Chance, increases Armor, and Increases Dodge

Intelligence increases Spell Damage. Intellect directly scales your Nature damage and deadly poisons, allowing your Damage-over-Time (DoT) effects and venom strikes to hit significantly harder.

Spell power increases Damage-over-Time (DoT) Spells: Scales the damage of your toxic poisons

Strength does give you attack power, but not as much as Agility.

entries.title: Boltslinger - Twilight Frenzy AoE
entries.description:
[overview]
This build specialises in AoE dungeon settings and is primarily using Twilight Frenzy for AoE and Witchbane for Single Target. If you've played Diablo III and enjoyed Demon Hunter, this could feel very familiar.
Build is highly effective provided the tank is pulling large packs of at least 3-4 mobs. Any less, and you won't have infinite rage to use Twilight Frenzy. 

**Pros:**
+High AoE capability
+Easy rotation
+High mobility
+AoE Stun/Silence

**Cons:**
-Spinning constantly
-Requires tank behaviour
-Poor survivability

## Abilities
**Spells used to deal damage: AoE**
1. Twilight Frenzy
2. Tormentor (with talent to spread it)
3. Caltrops
4. Shadow Trap
5. Scourge Frenzy

**Spells used to deal damage: Single Target**
1. Witchbane
2. Heartseeking Bolt
3. Tormentor
4. Scourge Trap
5. Shadow Trap
6. Death Trap
7. Brand of the Damned
8. Darkslayer

**Utility Spells:**
1. Shadow Trap - AoE stun (use to stabilise damage on tank)
2. Inquisitor's Trap - AoE silence (use on casters out of the pack) 
3. Caltrops - AoE slow (use to stabilise damage on tank)
4. Burrow Bolt - Drag that loose caster into the blender pack

**How to get more rage:**
1. Dark Regeneration
2. Tonics + Regenerative Elixirs talent in class tree
3. Darkslayer

[talents]
There are no Capstone talents for this build. The 25th point will go into Contract Killing. The majority of your casts will be Twilight Frenzy, and none of the Capstones play well with it during AoE sequences. You could pick up Bounty Hunter or Heavy Crossbows in its place for single target, but you'll get more out of Contract Killing overall in a dungeon setting.

**Tormentor + Strafing Shot:**
You can spread the Tormentor DoT to nearby enemies when you critically strike. This includes Twilight Frenzy. During AoE set up/the pull you can Darkslayer/Rage CD > Tormentor and then start Twilight Frenzy to spread. This will become even better when you hit level 50 (Tormenting the Tormented) and as you get more crit.

**Crossbow Frenzy:**
You will want the movement speed to keep up with certain tanks in a dungeon. Being able to catch up and use frenzy while the tank grabs more mobs to throw into the blender has very high potential damage.

**Everything you Have:**
More damage on Twilight Frenzy.

**Arbalest Mastery:**
On single target Witchbane is your main damage dealer. This will put a stacking debuff up to 10 on the target. Probably works with other WHs as well because it's a debuff on a target (ie Sunder). Get 50 rage and spam it. You can use Dark Regeneration/Tonics (with Regenerative Elixirs talent) to keep firing infinitely.

**Rapid:**
You don't need Witchbane to do AoE when you have Twilight Frenzy. Instead, make it Rapid so you can boost your boss and single target damage.

**Bane of Witches:**
Both Witchbane and Twilight Frenzy are physical damage. Heartseeking Arrow is primarily used on CD during Single Target for the +10% physical damage dealt. You may also get some use out of it as an effective filler cast while the tank is rounding up mobs and it isn't safe to Twilight Frenzy yet.

[rotation]
## AoE Rotation
While the tank grabs the mobs use Darkslayer once for rage or Heartseeking Bolt if you have more than 50 rage. Use Tormentor and then get ready to blend. Use Scourge/Shadow Trap once everything is stacked tight. Use Scourge Trap/Holy Water Tonic for undead/demons.

- Darkslayer/Heartseeking Bolt > Tormentor > Dark Regeneration/Holy Water Tonic > Twilight Frenzy until everything stacked > Scourge/Shadow Trap > Twilight Frenzy (until only 1 mob left)


## Single Target Rotation
You are keeping the Heartseeking Bolt +10% phys damage buff up on yourself, ensuring Tormentor is always ticking and using Witchbane as much as possible. Use your rage generators (tonics/Dark Regen) to avoid having to Darkslayer as required.

- Heartseeking Bolt > Tormentor > Dark Regeneration/Holy Water Tonic > Witchbane x6 > Refresh Tormentor + Caltrops > Refresh Heartseeking Bolt > Witchbane x6 > Refresh Tormentor

[macros]
**Twilight Frenzy:**
#showtooltip
/stopmacro [channeling:Twilight Frenzy]
/cast Twilight Frenzy
/stopcasting

**Caltrops:**
#showtooltip
/cast [mod:alt]Bola Throw;[@cursor]Caltrops

[tips]
Feeling overwhelmed by the amount of abilities? You can basically take Shadowblast off your bars.

You can cancel your Twilight Frenzy channel by using an instant cast.

Use your traps! The Scourge Trap is actually insane damage on Undead mobs and Brand of the Damned is basically a better Shadow Word: Death.

Some tanks get shitty when you start attacking before they've hit the mob. Just be aware and try to space yourself. If it's unsafe, don't Twilight Frenzy yet. Build some rage, get a Heartseeking buff. Ideally, the tank should be hitting the mobs as they run by so you can Twilight Frenzy almost immediately even as they continue to gather mobs up.
